title: Prevent migraine attacks through targeted CGRP-pathway treatment

concept.text: Reduce migraine frequency with medicines developed against a validated migraine pathway. Erenumab established the approved preventive antibody class; treatment reduces attacks rather than constituting a permanent cure. Proposed completion test: FDA approval for adult migraine prevention, supported by randomized trials showing superiority to placebo in monthly migraine days over 3–6 months and in the proportion achieving at least a 50% reduction. Test set by: FDA; the pivotal protocols prespecified monthly migraine days and 50%-responder endpoints. Reported achieved: FDA approved erenumab (Aimovig) on 17 May 2018. Sources given: [FDA Aimovig approval letter](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2018/761077Orig1s000Approv.pdf) ; [Aimovig prescribing information and trial outcomes](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/fda/fdaDrugXsl.cfm?setid=b998ed05-94b0-47fd-b28f-cddd1e128fd8&type=display).

page.title: First US approval of a CGRP-pathway medicine for migraine prevention in adults
page.definition: A medicine that blocks calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP), a nerve-signalling peptide, or the receptor through which it acts receives US approval for migraine prevention in adults. Preventive treatment aims to reduce the number of days with migraine during treatment. Erenumab, the first approved medicine in the class, blocks the receptor.

goal.need: About 40% of people with migraine qualify for preventive treatment, but only a minority of them use it. Side effects can make established medicines hard to continue. In a 24-week trial in adults with at least four migraine days a month, 10.6% stopped erenumab because of adverse events, compared with 38.9% on topiramate. During the final three months, 55.4% on erenumab cut their monthly migraine days by at least half, compared with 31.2% on topiramate.

statements.quote: The CGRP-targeting therapies should be considered as a first-line approach for migraine prevention
both are directed against a relatively new target in migraine prevention, the calcitonin gene-related peptide, or CGRP.
statements.context: The Academy described two phase 2 antibody trials scheduled for presentation at its 66th Annual Meeting.

statements.quote: do not tolerate or inadequately respond
statements.context: For nonpregnant adults receiving outpatient care for episodic migraine, the guideline suggests a CGRP-targeting medicine after a trial of metoprolol, propranolol, valproate, venlafaxine, or amitriptyline proves unsatisfactory.

completion.title: The FDA first approves a CGRP-pathway medicine for migraine prevention in adults.
completion.criterion: The FDA grants its first marketing approval for a medicine that blocks CGRP or its receptor and whose approved indication includes preventive treatment of migraine in adults. For each migraine subtype, the approved indication must cover that population.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, marketing approval and approved indication.
completion.threshold_quote: AIMOVIG is a calcitonin gene-related peptide receptor antagonist indicated for the preventive treatment of migraine in adults.
completion.basis: The FDA identified Aimovig (erenumab-aooe) as the first approved preventive in the class. Its approval took effect on 17 May 2018. The single adult migraine indication covers both episodic and chronic migraine. The FDA’s 2023 draft guidance recommends at least one adequate and well-controlled efficacy trial in each population to support an indication covering both.

milestones.title: An investigational new drug application takes effect for human testing of a CGRP-pathway medicine.
milestones.criterion: The investigational new drug application includes pharmacology and toxicology information supporting the sponsor’s conclusion that the proposed human investigation is reasonably safe. The application takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt unless the FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if the FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8) and 312.40(b), (d).
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: A CGRP-pathway medicine reaches initial human dosing in a phase 1 study.
milestones.criterion: Administer the investigational CGRP-pathway medicine to a human participant for the first time in a phase 1 study. The study may enrol healthy volunteers or patients and assesses safety and human pharmacology.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, phase 1 definition in 21 CFR 312.21(a); this human-dosing stage is shared by both migraine cases.
milestones.threshold_quote: Phase 1 includes the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: A CGRP-pathway medicine reduces monthly migraine days versus placebo in a phase 2 trial.
milestones.criterion: Show superiority to placebo on the prespecified phase 2 primary endpoint of change from baseline in monthly migraine days. Both erenumab protocols assess weeks 9–12 of 12 weeks of double-blind treatment. The episodic trial tests 70, 21, then 7 mg monthly at two-sided α = 0.05, proceeding to each lower dose only if the preceding comparison succeeds. The chronic trial initially tests 70 mg at α = 0.04 and 140 mg at α = 0.01 under its prespecified multiplicity procedure.
milestones.set_by: Amgen, protocols NCT01952574 for episodic migraine and NCT02066415 for chronic migraine, described in their primary publications. The quoted endpoint is from the episodic-migraine protocol.
milestones.threshold_quote: the change in monthly migraine days from baseline to the last 4 weeks of the 12-week double-blind treatment phase.

milestones.title: A CGRP-pathway medicine meets a phase 3 primary superiority test against placebo for migraine prevention.
milestones.criterion: Show superiority to placebo on the prespecified phase 3 primary endpoint. For episodic migraine, STRIVE tests change from baseline in mean monthly migraine days over months 4–6, at α = 0.04 for erenumab 70 mg and α = 0.01 for 140 mg. For chronic migraine, HALO tests change from baseline in mean monthly qualifying headache days over 12 weeks using hierarchical comparisons at two-sided α = 0.05. A day qualifies with at least four consecutive hours of pain reaching at least moderate intensity, or with triptan or ergot use for headache of any severity or duration.
milestones.set_by: Amgen and Novartis, STRIVE protocol NCT02456740 for episodic migraine; Teva Pharmaceuticals, HALO protocol NCT02621931 for chronic migraine. The quoted significance thresholds apply to STRIVE.
milestones.threshold_quote: at an alpha level of 0.04 for 70 mg and of 0.01 for 140 mg.

milestones.title: A candidate medicine inhibits a response to CGRP in a laboratory assay.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate in a functional assay that the candidate inhibits a response elicited by CGRP. The assay may test neutralization of the peptide or antagonism of its receptor. Compare the response in the presence and absence of the candidate.
milestones.set_by: International Conference on Harmonisation, M3(R2), section 2, on primary pharmacodynamic studies of a candidate’s action at its intended target.
milestones.threshold_quote: intended to investigate the mode of action and/or effects of a substance in relation to its desired therapeutic target.

milestones.title: The FDA accepts a marketing application for review for CGRP-targeted migraine prevention.
milestones.criterion: The FDA files a new drug application or biologics license application for a CGRP-pathway medicine with a proposed indication that includes migraine prevention in adults. The filing decision establishes that the application can proceed to substantive review.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research, Manual of Policies and Procedures 6025.4.
milestones.threshold_quote: If the application is complete for review, the application will be filed.
